title: Software Engineer, Early Career 2027
reason: Stack +68; Synergy +6; Title fit +12; Entry +15; US +10
description_preview:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.
Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”
Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.
The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.
About The Role
We're looking for early career Software Engineers to join our engineering team. You'll work alongside experienced engineers across backend, frontend, mobile, and infrastructure, while owning meaningful production systems and product features from the beginning.
Role
This is a role for someone who wants to learn quickly, take on significant responsibility, and build systems used by clinicians every day. Team placement will vary, but examples could include:
AI & Agents:
Build an AI-powered workflow that helps healthcare teams automate repetitive administrative work.
Clinical:
Develop features that help clinicians spend less time documenting and more time with patients.
Revenue Cycle Management:
Build software that helps healthcare practices automate billing workflows and improve their financial operations.
Platform & Infrastructure:
Improve the reliability, observability, or scalability of services supporting thousands of healthcare organizations.
Product Engineering:
Build end-to-end features across React, APIs, backend services, and databases that are used by healthcare providers every day.
What You’ll Do
Building product features across our web, mobile, and backend applications, including offline-first experiences for healthcare professionals
Developing reliable APIs and backend services that support high-volume clinical workflows
Building data processing pipelines for handling complex, high-volume healthcare data
Building and improving AI systems: inference pipelines, orchestration (fallbacks, retries, async workflows), and quality evaluation infrastructure
Improving monitoring, observability, alerting, debugging, and overall application performance, reliability, and stability
Designing internal tools that make engineers faster and production systems easier to operate
Working directly with product, design, clinical, and customer-facing teams to understand real-world problems and ship solutions
What You Have
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, graduating recently or within the upcoming academic year
Strong fundamentals in algorithms, data structures, operating systems, databases, networking, or distributed systems
Experience building software through internships, research, open-source projects, coursework, startups, or personal projects—ideally something substantial outside of coursework
Ability to write clean, understandable, and maintainable code
Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, especially across multiple layers of a system
Curiosity about how complex systems work beyond the component you are directly working on
Care about reliability and performance, not just getting a feature to work once
High ownership—you care about whether the thing you built actually works for users in production
Willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies and move quickly
Prefer ownership and autonomy over narrowly scoped tickets
Want to work close to users and see the impact of your work quickly
Strong communication and ability to work closely with engineers and non-engineers
Our Technical Environment
You May Work With Technologies Including
Languages & Frameworks: Python, TypeScript, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React, and native mobile platforms
Infrastructure & Data: PostgreSQL, Redis, cloud object storage, Kubernetes, containers, distributed queues, and data processing pipelines
AI Systems: LLM inference and orchestration pipelines, AI evaluation infrastructure
Observability & Testing: Monitoring, logging, tracing, production observability, and automated testing
Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in
@
commure.com
. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.
Employees will act in accordance with the organization’s information security policies, to include but not limited to protecting assets from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or interference nor execute particular security processes or activities. Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.
Compensation Range: $130K - $150K

Company Overview
Join Seerist, a leading provider of AI-driven, augmented analytics for threat and risk intelligence, designed to help commercial organizations and government anticipate, monitor, and manage global risks. Seerist delivers real-time insights, forecasts, and alerts that bring clarity to decisions and save valuable time for security and intelligence teams. Every day, Seerist helps our customers support their operations and missions globally, ensuring informed, rapid decisions.
About The Role
You will join the Collections & Alerts software development team to build the platform's data ingestion and processing infrastructure. Your pipelines power real-time intelligence; when they fail, customers notice. You'll design and build high-volume data pipelines, architect event-driven systems that process intelligence data at scale, optimize queries and schemas for heavy load, instrument services for observability, and debug production issues across distributed systems. You'll work directly with our intelligence analysts and product team to understand requirements and ensure software meets both performance and analytical needs.
Technical Skills Required
Languages: Experience with TypeScript, Node.js, Python, and other modern languages
Event-Driven Architecture: Experience designing and debugging event-driven systems (EventBridge, message queues, async patterns, orchestration)
Data Pipelines: Experience building high-volume, low-latency data ingestion and processing pipelines; understanding of batch vs. real-time tradeoffs
AWS: Hands-on work with SQS, S3, ECR, AWS CDK; comfortable reasoning about cloud infrastructure costs and scaling
Databases: Working knowledge of both relational (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (DynamoDB); experience optimizing queries and schema design for high-volume workloads
Search & Caching: Experience with in-memory data stores (Redis), familiarity with OpenSearch/ElasticSearch (full-text search, indexing strategies)
Monitoring & Observability: Proficiency with Datadog or similar monitoring tools; ability to instrument code for observability and debug production issues
Microservices: Understanding of service boundaries, async communication patterns, and debugging across distributed systems
Infrastructure as Code: Comfortable with AWS CDK or similar tools for defining infrastructure in code
Coding agents: Comfortable leveraging AI tooling for development acceleration, building custom skills, and automating repetitive tasks.
What Seerist Offers:
An opportunity to be a part of a fast-moving organization with cutting edge technology
A culture that is dynamic, diverse, trust-centered, and open to bold ideas
Competitive salary, bonus plan, 401(k) matching, and long-term incentives
Comprehensive benefits including health, dental, vision, and life plans
A flexible and fun work environment that values work-life balance
Hybrid position with 3 days in office per week and flexibility to work onsite as the program requires
Unlimited PTO
Up to 16 Weeks Paid Parental Leave
Tuition Reimbursement
Professional Development Stipend
Based in the greater Washington, DC metro area, in our Reston office three days per week, with the flexibility to work on site as the program requires

Charity Navigator is the world's largest and most-utilized independent nonprofit evaluator. The organization guides informed giving by evaluating the financial health, accountability, transparency, and impact of charities and provides data on over 245,000 nonprofits. As a 501(c)(3) public charity itself, Charity Navigator depends on support from individuals, corporations, and foundations to provide this trusted data free of charge to the public.
The Role
You will build and ship production LLM-powered and agentic features that make 2.4 million nonprofit profiles easier to search, compare, and understand - so a donor gets a clear answer instead of a spreadsheet.
This is application-layer work. You will partner with our existing engineering team rather than owning the pipelines yourself, so your time goes into the AI features people use.
You will report to the VP of Engineering and work closely with them and other senior engineers on system design, technical direction, and strategic AI opportunities. You will own AI features from day one, with regular design review and hands-on guidance on the harder architectural calls, and take on more architectural ownership as you build depth in production AI systems.
What You'll Do
Build and ship production LLM-powered and agentic features - prompt orchestration, tool calling, embeddings, structured outputs - favoring reusable components over one-off solutions.
Build API Integrations, MCP servers, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows that connect our existing data systems to vector search, so that AI features surface and explain our published ratings data accurately and cite the source of each figure.
Build and run evaluation infrastructure - prompt regression tests, LLM-as-a-judge evaluations, synthetic datasets - that catch feature quality regressions before users do.
Monitor AI features in production. Track accuracy, latency, token cost, and hallucination rates, then debug and tune prompts based on what you find.
Implement runtime safety and reliability guardrails that keep AI outputs within quality, compliance, and operational bounds.
Research and recommend orchestration frameworks, vector stores, and model providers, weighing cost and operational burden against speed. Final build-versus-buy calls are made jointly with the VP of Engineering.
Work directly with non-technical stakeholders to scope problems and give them honest assessments of what AI can and cannot do.
Evaluate emerging models and tools, use AI-assisted development extensively, and help raise team engineering standards through code review.

Resourcefulness and adaptability.
You learn quickly against unfamiliar problems, new ideas, and changing technology, and you find a way through when the obvious path is blocked.

Direct, truthful communication. You keep your commitments, admit mistakes and correct them, and give peers respectful, open-minded feedback.

Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.
We're hiring
Full Stack Software Engineers graduating between December 2026 and June 2027
to join our engineering team in Miami, starting May or June 2027. This is not a rotational program and it isn't a shadowing role. You'll join one of our product squads and work across the whole stack — from the data model through the API to the interface a patient or a care navigator actually uses. Our engineering team is around twenty people, which means the work you ship is visibly yours and the distance between your code and a patient getting a scan scheduled is very short.
It also means you'll be building alongside a team that has moved unusually early on AI-assisted engineering. We run a shared AI harness that every engineer's agent builds on, we have AI agents running in production behind guardrails and eval suites, and we're explicit internally that writing code is no longer the slow part of the job — the slow parts are deciding what to build and verifying what comes out. Build and ship full stack features across our React frontend and TypeScript/Node.js backend, with a senior engineer as your mentor and reviewer

Work with AI coding agents as a normal part of your workflow, and take full accountability for the output: you should be able to explain every file in your diff
Write tests across the stack, and treat verification as part of shipping rather than a phase afterwards
Participate in design reviews and code reviews from your first weeks — including reviewing other engineers' work, because a bare approval with no comment isn't a completed review here
Ask why. We reason from first principles and we have an explicit norm that engineers are not implementation machines — if a requirement doesn't make sense, we want you to say so
Build features that handle protected health information correctly, with authentication, authorization, and audit logging as first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts
About you:
Graduating with a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline between December 2026 and June 2027
You've built things nobody assigned you — side projects, hackathon work, open-source contributions, something with real users, however few
Working knowledge of JavaScript or TypeScript, and comfort with either React or Node.js. We care much more about how you reason than about which technologies you've already used
Familiarity with relational databases and SQL, and a basic mental model of how a web request becomes a database query
You use AI coding tools and you've formed opinions about them — including where they mislead you and how you catch it
You can explain a technical decision you made and what you'd do differently, which matters more to us than the sophistication of the project
Comfortable with ambiguity and with being told "we haven't figured that out yet"
Intellectually honest: you can change your mind when the evidence changes, and you'd rather delete your own work than defend it
Clear written and verbal communication — you'll be writing design docs and PR descriptions that other people depend on
Authorized to work in the United States, and able to be based in Miami
Nice to have, and genuinely not required:
An internship or co-op where you shipped to production
Experience with PostgreSQL, Express, or a typed API layer
Anything you've built on top of LLM or agent APIs — tools, harnesses, evals, agents
Testing experience with Jest, Vitest, Playwright, or similar
Exposure to AWS or another cloud provider
Curiosity about healthcare data standards (FHIR, HL7, DICOM) — we'll teach you these, and we'd rather you question how things are done in radiology than arrive already knowing
A background in accessibility or internationalization
What we'll give you
A published career framework with written promotion criteria, so you can see the path from Associate Software Engineer through Senior, Staff and Principal, and know exactly what's expected at each step. A mentor from among our senior engineers, for whom mentorship is a written part of their job. Real ownership, quickly. And a mission that's easy to get behind with real life impact.

: Help build and scale the tooling we use to measure how well AI-powered software development tools perform. This is an engineering role, but a lot of the work is about getting the measurement right, not just automating it.
Key Responsibilities
• Build and integrate evaluation harnesses and automation for software development use cases, including turning real engineering artifacts like merged pull requests into repeatable benchmark tasks.

• Analyze results across repeated runs, looking at variance, failure patterns, and cost per outcome, and find ways to make the workflows more reliable and more automated.
• Work with engineering and data teams to improve the tooling, and document how the evaluations work and what they found for both technical and leadership audiences.

• Experience with APIs, development environments, CI/CD pipelines, and typical engineering workflows.
• Understanding of how AI, LLM, or agent evaluation works and where it goes wrong, such as why a judge can be consistent but still wrong, why a single run can mislead, and how
benchmark contamination happens.
• Able to troubleshoot technical problems, think clearly about whether a measurement is valid, and analyze results carefully.
• Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agentic harnesses such as Claude Code, Devin, or Cursor, and command of the best practices for working with them effectively.

• Familiarity with LLM-as-judge or agent-as-judge approaches, and how to check them against human raters.
• Experience with build-system-aware test selection, such as Bazel or mapping changed files to the tests that cover them.
• Experience building reproducible test environments and managing versioned evaluation datasets.
• Comfortable writing up methodology and results for engineering leadership.
Notes from the Manager:
They must have experience using existing AI tools with harnesses such as Claude, Devin, Cursor etc. and the best practices using them. Evaluation and benchmarking experience (getting the measurement right, not just automating it). Solid working knowledge of Git, including how branches, history, and working trees behave, and of containerization with Docker.
The intention is to renew every 6 months, and if FTE positions become available contractors will be considered first
Must work Pacific Time zone. Not accepting candidates with more than a two-hour difference.

description_preview:
About the Role
You’ll join the team that owns AIDR’s core reasoning engine — the multi-agent layer that turns telemetry from 70+ security vendors into investigated, correlated conclusions an analyst can act on. You’ll design the agent architectures, run the experiments that decide which ones ship, and take them into production environments where SOC teams depend on the output. Success is measured in precision, recall, latency, and cost, not demo quality.
That standard shapes how we work:
Accuracy and honesty. We’re clear about what we’ve measured versus what’s still a hypothesis. We expect the same of your results — including when one doesn’t hold up.
Research into production. We move new research into the product quickly, then validate it against operational standards rather than demo conditions.
Measure, then decide. We experiment in small increments and make calls from metrics, not intuition.
In practice, you’ll spend as much time building the evaluation harnesses that tell us whether an agent is good as you will building the agent itself. If you want to work on LLM systems where “is it good?” has a number attached, this is that role.
What you’ll do
Build our multi-agent LLM system: Design and improve the core system where multiple LLM agents collaborate to detect, investigate, and correlate threats.
LLM orchestration: Build pipelines that coordinate multiple models against cost, latency, and accuracy trade-offs based on the task.
Evaluation & continuous improvement: Create the evaluation systems that measure agent output quality, and design the loops that feed operational data back as a learning signal.
Reliability: Experiment with and ship prompting, architecture, and verification strategies that reduce hallucination and improve stability and reproducibility.
Build what’s next: Go beyond investigation into automated response, deeper threat correlation, and new product areas that push security operations further — built from the ground up, with you.
Minimum Qualifications
Hands-on experience designing and building LLM applications (agents, RAG, orchestration, etc.)
Strong software engineering fundamentals in Python
Experience building LLM workflows with various agent frameworks
Experience evaluating and improving LLM output quality, both qualitatively and quantitatively — a real instinct for measurement, not just implementation
Comfort defining ambiguous problems, experimenting quickly, and making decisions from data

Experience designing evaluations/benchmarks, or an ML research background (publications, open source contributions, etc.)
Experience operating production LLM systems (monitoring, cost optimization, latency management)
Experience deploying production systems across cloud environments

title: Software Engineer
reason: Stack +10; Title fit +12; Exp fit +10; US +10; Senior desc -15
description_preview:
Moog is a performance culture that empowers people to achieve great things. Our people enjoy solving interesting technical challenges in a culture where everyone trusts each other to do the right thing. For you, working with us can mean deeper job satisfaction, better rewards, and a great quality of life inside and outside of work.
Job Title
Software Engineer
Reporting To
Software Engineering Manager
Work Schedule
Onsite – Phoenix, AZ
Mission & Impact
Join a team that develops embedded software for flight spacecraft systems and single board computers (SBCs). You’ll develop board support packages, bring up hardware, and create device drivers for new interfaces on VxWorks and other embedded platforms—from design through integration and verification.
Bring your strong C/C++ (and scripting) real-time embedded development and hands-on debugging skills, and apply your software engineering expertise alongside Moog-specific tools, platforms, and devices.
You do not need every preferred skill to apply; strong candidates typically meet ~80% and show willingness to learn.
What You’ll Do
Develop embedded avionics software: implement and maintain C/C++ software on single board computers (SBCs) and real-time operating systems (VxWorks 6/7).
Board bring-up & low-level drivers: support SBC bring-up and develop/debug software drivers for serial interfaces (SPI, I2C, UART), Ethernet, and high-speed links (LVDS/differential pairs), including SpaceWire (PHY/MAC) and MIL-STD-1553 as applicable.
Integrate with hardware and systems: collaborate with electrical, systems, and test teams to integrate software with custom analog/digital I/O, watchdog timers, and processor peripherals; troubleshoot issues across HW/SW boundaries.
Verification & test: derive test requirements, create unit and regression tests, support integration testing, and debug anomalies using logs, telemetry, and lab equipment.
Technical reviews & program execution: participate in peer and code/design reviews; support major program reviews and required technical data deliverables.
Configuration management & release: use version control to manage branches and baselines, support software/document releases, and track work and defects in Jira (including bug triage).
Documentation: produce and maintain user guides, software design documentation, and release notes; contribute to formal document release processes.
Must Have Qualifications (Core)
2+ years of professional embedded software development experience (aerospace/defense preferred).
Proficiency in C/C++ for real-time/embedded systems.
Experience with RTOS development and debugging.
BSP/device-driver experience.
Working knowledge of serial communications (SPI/I2C/UART) and debugging at the protocol level.
Experience with software troubleshooting and root-cause analysis across HW/SW interfaces.
Familiarity with the end-to-end software development process: requirements, design, implementation, peer review, unit testing, regression testing, configuration management, and release.
Experience using version control (Git/Perforce preferred) and issue tracking (e.g., Jira).
Ability to produce clear technical documentation (user guides, design notes) and communicate effectively in peer-to-peer engineering settings.
U.S. person (due to export controlled work).
Nice to Have (We Will Train Where Needed)
VxWorks 6.x / 7.x experience; Wind River Workbench.
Experience with spacecraft/avionics SBCs and bring-up.
SpaceWire (PHY/MAC/cabling) and/or MIL-STD-1553 experience.
Static code analysis tools and secure coding practices.
Familiarity with Perforce, Bitbucket, and formal release/baseline processes.
Experience supporting formal program reviews (SRR/PDR/CDR/TRR) and deliverables.
Growth & Development
Structured onboarding with mentorship and exposure to multiple spacecraft programs.
Targeted training on Moog-specific architectures, tools, and program processes.
Clear technical progression toward lead embedded software roles and mentoring responsibilities.
Salary Range Transparency
Phoenix, AZ $75,000.00–$120,000.00 Annually
Salary Range Disclaimer
The base salary range represents the low and high end of the Moog salary range for this position in the given work location. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range(s) listed is just one component of Moog's total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, employee stock purchase plan, an open paid time off policy, and many region-specific benefits.
This position requires access to U.S. export-controlled information.

About Levelpath
Backed by some of the top venture capital firms in Silicon Valley and founded by third-time founders with two successful exits, Levelpath is building autonomous procurement.
We've built an agentic software factory that accelerates our development by an order of magnitude. Everything we learn about harnessing AI to build software goes into the product, driving faster, more accurate, and safer outcomes for enterprise procurement teams. We build with the aggressive assumption that everything in procurement can be done by AI. Our job is to prove it.
Autonomy only counts when it connects to the systems an enterprise already runs. Nothing makes Levelpath real for a customer faster than the moment their ERP, HRIS, and financial systems start talking to us. That moment is this job.
The role
You will own the connective tissue between Levelpath and the systems our customers already run: ERPs like NetSuite, SAP, and Oracle, plus HRIS, SSO, ticketing, e-signature, and finance tools. Some integrations you build yourself. Others are built by customer teams, and you are the engineer who guides them, unblocks them, and makes sure everything works in production.
This is a customer-facing engineering role in the truest sense. You will be on calls with customer IT and integration teams, whiteboarding data flows, debugging auth handshakes live, and turning ambiguous requirements into working pipelines. When a customer's integration engineer is stuck, you are the person who gets them moving again.
You will build with our agentic software factory, and you will improve it. The factory is optimized for exactly this work: well-specified contracts and a premium on verification. It is not perfect, and when it falls short you fix the cause, contributing tooling back so the next integration ships faster. Agents are the execution capacity here. Your job is to drive them to the outcome: unblock them when they stall, correct them when they drift, and verify what they ship.
You will also be the engineering presence in the US timezone. Our core platform team is distributed internationally, and you help anchor US-hours on-call coverage so customers get a fast, expert response no matter when things break. On-call is a real part of this role, and we invest in the observability, runbooks, and agent tooling that make it sane.
What you will do
Design, build, and ship integrations between Levelpath and enterprise systems (ERP, HRIS, SSO/SCIM, ticketing, e-signature) using TypeScript, NestJS, and PostgreSQL in an agent-driven workflow.
Lead technical calls with customer engineering and IT teams: scoping, architecture reviews, debugging sessions, and go-live support.
Guide customers building against our GraphQL API and MCP surface, from first webhook to production cutover.
Harden integration paths for the realities of enterprise data: schema enforcement, validation, retries, idempotency, and graceful degradation.
Anchor US-hours on-call, triaging production issues and improving the tooling that makes the next incident easier.
Feed what you learn in the field back into the product: better connectors, better docs, better defaults.
What you bring
Solid backend or full-stack fundamentals with several years shipping production software.
Real experience with third-party APIs and integration work: REST and GraphQL, webhooks, OAuth and SAML flows, data mapping, and the patience to read someone else's API docs carefully.
AI-pilled, genuinely. Your instinct is to hand work to agents first, and you want to turn over as much as possible to AI, in your own workflow and in the product. You have the judgment to know when it worked.
A deep-seated need to ship. We believe we win by outshipping everyone, and we hire engineers who treat blockers as things to bulldoze, not things to wait on.
Ownership by default. No one here is just on a team. Everyone owns and leads something, and you should want that.
TypeScript and Node.js experience (NestJS a plus). We care more about fundamentals than exact-stack trivia.
PostgreSQL knowledge and comfort with Docker.
An incredible attitude. You genuinely enjoy customer calls, you stay calm when production is on fire, and teammates describe you as the person they want in the room when things get hard.
Excellent communication, written and verbal. You can explain a webhook retry policy to a customer's IT admin and a data model tradeoff to our platform team with equal clarity.
Nice to have
Experience with enterprise procurement, finance, or ERP ecosystems (Ariba, Coupa, NetSuite, SAP, Workday).
Experience with iPaaS platforms or building connector frameworks.

Top salary and equity
AI-paced culture
A team that plays like pros: high standards, high growth, no passengers
Ability to have strong customer context and autonomy
401K, Medical, Dental and Vision insurance

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
OUR TEAM
Within Anduril, our team develops unmanned aerial systems capable of terminal guidance, long range intelligence collection, precision navigation, and unsupervised autonomy. Anvil, Altius, Ghost, and other developmental UAS platforms operate in remote environments with limited user input, driving requirements for reliability and autonomy. We have developed an autonomy stack that receives user intent, responds to detections processed at the edge, and coordinates flight patterns for groups of assets. We want systems engineers with experience in this field to help design and manage the next generation of Anduril’s flight vehicles. In order to succeed at Anduril, a systems engineer needs familiarity with simulation and rapid prototyping development to drive complex electro-mechanical and aero-performance design trades, in addition to supporting the engineering product development, production, and sustainment through the entire product lifecycle.
What You’ll Do
Lead development for an end-to-end solution by collaborating with cross-functional teams to define requirements and system architecture
Design, develop, and maintain system components that meet functional and performance requirements in complex system environments
Conduct thorough testing and debugging to ensure the reliability, scalability, and resilience of software applications, especially within a distributed systems context
Work closely with hardware engineers and product managers to ensure seamless integration of software and hardware components
Collaborate with the team to define and document software engineering processes and practices, ensuring adherence to quality standards and regulatory requirements
Required Qualifications
A passion for systems design, development, integration, and testing
2-6 years of industry experience including but not limited to electrical engineering, aerospace engineering or systems engineering
Comfort with systems modeling tools such as Cameo
Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies and the ability to operate effectively in an Agile development environment
Hands-on prototyping, troubleshooting, and build experience of complex robotic systems
Experience developing automated test scripts and frameworks using a common language (eg, Python, MATLAB, etc)
Extremely organized and detail-oriented, and excellent verbal & written communication skills
A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
Ability to obtain a U.S. security clearance
Ability to travel domestically up to 25% as needed for test planning and execution, and excitement to work onsite at our headquarters in Costa Mesa, CA the rest of the time!
Preferred Qualifications
Hands-on experience with prototyping, troubleshooting, and building complex robotic systems
Familiarity with IP- based networks
Experience with mission systems to include communications systems and components
Familiarity with aviation airworthiness considerations
Already hold a U.S. Secret security clearance, or higher

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.
For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com

Design and Integrate Systems for Mission Success
Bluestaq is hiring a Delivery Engineer to operate and evolve our Kubernetes-based platform on AWS. You will own the deployment automation, day-to-day production health, and incident response for the services that power the Unified Data Library (UDL) — a mission-critical data platform used across government and commercial space operations.

Why This Role Matters
Bluestaq delivers integrated, secure, and reliable systems for customers operating in mission-critical and commercially demanding environments. Systems engineering is at the core of how we win, deliver, and scale. Without strong systems engineering execution, our teams can't move fast, our systems can't stay secure, and our customers can't rely on the technology that supports their operations.
This role is foundational to the team and the organization. Your work spans defined features, environments, and components within a team, with growing independence, which means your decisions, your designs, and your technical judgment have a direct and measurable effect on what Bluestaq delivers. Automate repetitive operational toil using Python, Bash, or PowerShell

Amazon Leo is a initiative within Amazon that aims to revolutionize global connectivity through the development of a state-of-the-art Low Earth Orbit (LEO) interconnected satellite communication constellation. Our mission is to bridge the digital divide by delivering high-speed, low latency, internet services to underserved and unserved communities and remote communities around the world. By leveraging satellite technology, we are working towards a future where everyone has access to reliable and high-quality internet connectivity regardless of their location.
The Amazon Leo for Government (ALG) Engineering organization is a multi-disciplinary technology team established to rapidly address the needs of targeted government and international customers with specific solutions that have the potential to scale. ALG Engineering leads the development and delivery of targeted and scalable solutions for custom space and terrestrial applications. ALG collaborates closely with Project LEO to leverage the constellation of advance satellites to provide seamless and efficient communication capabilities to meet the needs of our customers. The ALG Engineering team is seeking highly technical and talented individuals who are passionate about creating unique solutions that result in a positive impact on a global scale.
About The Role
The Software Integration & Test (I&T) Engineer will engage with an experienced cross-disciplinary team to design, develop, and own software tooling and frameworks that enable integration testing within system lab environments for space-based and terrestrial applications. This role sits at the intersection of software engineering and systems verification — you will define how teams test, not just what they test.
Working within Amazon Leo for Government (ALG) Engineering Integrated Systems Solutions, you will architect and deliver reusable test platforms, automation frameworks, and lab infrastructure software that accelerate verification of complex integrated hardware and software systems. You will serve as the technical owner of lab tooling strategy, driving decisions on architecture, interfaces, and developer experience while collaborating across inter-disciplinary teams, partners, and suppliers.
The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience working on complex Hardware/Software systems with a diverse set of talented individuals, as well as with partner organizations.

Own the design, development, and long-term health of test automation frameworks, orchestration platforms, and CI/CD-integrated tooling consumed by I&T engineers and subsystem teams in hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and system lab environments
Architect, design, and validate software tooling — including test algorithms, scripts, calibration routines, and data visualization — required for verification and validation of complex hardware systems
Define and drive tooling best practices across the lab engineering organization, establishing patterns for automation, observability, and infrastructure-as-code that raise the bar for the broader team
Analyze test data and engage cross-functionally with teammates, partners, suppliers, and customers to evaluate product performance and provide proactive feedback on potential improvements

Mentor junior engineers on software development practices, code quality, and test automation design patterns
Collaborate with systems engineers, hardware teams, and external partners to ensure tooling supports all phases of integration, test, verification, and validation across satellite and ground element campaigns

Mid-level electrical engineer responsible for designing, developing, and supporting electrical and electronic systems for industrial and maritime products. The role focuses on PCB and circuit design, motor control systems, industrial networking, and producing detailed documentation (one-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, ECNs/ECOs). The engineer will participate in design reviews, DFMEA and DVT activities, support manufacturing and field commissioning, and collaborate with mechanical, firmware, and systems teams to deliver reliable, compliant products.

Design and develop schematics and PCB layouts for embedded and industrial control systems, ensuring manufacturability and testability.

Develop, troubleshoot, and document motor control systems including VFD selection/integration, starters, and protective devices.
Author and maintain one-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, panel layouts, and detailed panel wiring instructions for production and field service.
Program and troubleshoot PLC ladder logic and related control sequences; work with Siemens, Allen-Bradley or equivalent platforms as required.
Design and integrate industrial networking solutions using RS-485, RS-232, CANbus, Fieldbus and Ethernet technologies; perform network diagnostics and commissioning.
Lead DFMEA and participate in DVT/validation testing; plan and execute electrical test procedures and support lab debug activities.
Prepare and manage ECNs/ECOs, maintain accurate BOMs, and update technical documentation to support design changes and manufacturing releases.
Collaborate with embedded/firmware engineers to ensure electrical and software interfaces are robust and validated.
Support production handoff, supplier selection and evaluation, and provide technical assistance during assembly and field commissioning, including maritime deployments.
Ensure designs meet applicable industry and maritime standards and assist with certification activities as required.
Mentor junior engineers and technicians; contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and cross-functional design reviews.
Qualifications
Bachelors degree in Electrical Engineering (or equivalent) required.
4+ years of practical experience in electrical design; mid-level (Electrical Engineer II) or similar role preferred.
Proven experience with PCB design tools (e.g., Altium, OrCAD, Eagle) and schematic capture/layout workflows.
Strong circuit design skills, including power electronics, signal conditioning and embedded power distribution.
Hands-on experience with motor controls, VFDs, panel wiring, and creating one-line and wiring diagrams.
Experience programming or troubleshooting PLC ladder logic and industrial controls.
Familiarity with industrial networking protocols and interfaces: RS-485, RS-232, CANbus, Fieldbus, and general Ethernet-based networks.
Experience with ECN/ECO processes, DFMEA, and participating in DVT or validation testing.
Exposure to marine or maritime systems and related compliance/certification requirements is strongly preferred.
Embedded design experience or close collaboration with firmware teams is desired.
Proficient with test equipment (oscilloscopes, power analyzers, multimeters) and comfortable performing bench-level debug.
Excellent technical communication skills, ability to work cross-functionally, and willingness to travel to customer or field sites as needed.
Professional Engineer (PE) or relevant certifications and experience with safety and quality systems (ISO, IPC) are a plus.
